#2086. Birmingham City man’s impressive display offers Chris Davies a new selection headache ahead of Bolton Wanderers tie: Opinion

Birmingham City sit 4th in the league after 17 matches and they are not showing signs of slowing down. BCFC won comfortably against a poor Burnley side last night to take their tally for the season to 32 points.

The most impressive part of Blues’ resurgence this season is their away form, as they have already matched their away win total from last season – and it is only November.

This was a huge reason that Chris Davies‘ side fell short of reaching the Championship play-offs last season. A big part of the improvements on the road this term has been the defence. The Blues have conceded the fewest goals in the Championship and kept a sixth clean sheet of the season against Burnley.

On Wednesday, they did so without captain and standout centre-back Christoph Klarer due to suspension. With Dael Fry alongside Phil Neumann, Birmingham City looked just as solid at the back.

There were some questions over how the Blues would handle missing their captain against Burnley after he picked up a suspension against Stoke City. However, Dael Fry was an ideal replacement for Klarer.

Fry has struggled for game time since leaving Middlesbrough. He hadn’t started in the league up until Birmingham City’s match at Turf Moor.

The 29-year-old has had to bide his time due to Klarer and Neumann forming such a strong partnership this season, and despite this, Fry slotted into the backline perfectly. The former Boro mainstay provided the physicality and no-nonsense defending to make him an ideal partner for Neumann’s speed and ball-playing ability.

Fry was a force in both boxes as he constantly won headers in attack and defence. He won three of his five duels total and was assured in possession with 41 passes completed, seven of which were into the final third (FotMob). He showed that despite his lack of game time, he is still a top defender at the level.

BCFC were praised for signing Fry on a free in the summer due to his experience, and he looks as though he will still have an important role to play in the Blues’ promotion push this season.

Birmingham City have had to make a lot of changes this season due to injuries and suspensions. However, they have looked strong no matter who is playing.

There was a clear focus on depth in the summer window. So far, at points, Carlos Vicente, Paik Seung-ho, Max Bird, Ryan Allsop, Ethan Laird and Dael Fry have all had to come in the starting lineup to replace first-choice players this season.

Having top Championship players like coming in as backup options is a huge weapon for the Blues. Fry would be the first choice at centre-back for a lot of sides in this league.

This depth could really help Birmingham City in a promotion push this season, but it gives Davies a tough call on how best to manage Fry, as a player of his quality is sure to be eager to play more football.

Fry is a professional who can contribute away from the pitch, but his quality is clear to see, and it deserves to be on show. Davies will be more than aware of this, and he will simply encourage the player to prove he deserves to find more minutes when the chances arise.

It is harsh, but Fry likely drops out of the BCFC side for Saturday’s clash with Bolton Wanderers. Davies will have to manage the situation carefully to keep everyone happy and motivated.

#2085. West Bromwich Albion vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:09, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:54

Looking to gain ground in the race for automatic promotion, West Bromwich Albion welcome Bristol City to The Hawthorns for a Championship contest on Saturday afternoon.

The Baggies are in the midst of an impressive unbeaten run in the second tier, making them the favourites with the best UK betting apps 2026 to record victory over the out-of-form Robins.

Since a 1-0 defeat by Birmingham City at The Hawthorns on October 10, West Brom have strung together an eight-game unbeaten streak (W5 D3) in the Championship, beating Bolton Wanderers last time out.

Wednesday night's match at the Toughsheet Community Stadium provided the stage for Albion's Norwegian stars to shine, with Aune Heggebo (2) and Felix Horn Myhre scoring in a 3-1 success over the Wanderers.

Now boasting the best away record in the division with 17 points collected from nine outings, James Morrison's side are back at The Hawthorns this weekend, when they will be striving for a repeat of their 3-0 battering of Millwall in the Black Country prior to the international break.

One of four Midlands clubs inside the top five of the Championship standings after 17 matches, West Brom are occupying fifth spot in the table, just three points behind pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke City.

Scoring an eye-catching eight goals across their past three league fixtures, the Baggies pose danger from an array of positions, with five different players scoring three or more Championship goals so far this term.

Following three consecutive losses at the beginning of their tricky November schedule, Bristol City stopped the rot with a respectable 1-1 draw with Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night.

It looked as if the Robins were hurtling towards their ninth defeat of the league campaign when Joe Worrall opened the scoring early on, but Cameron Pring's first goal in nearly three years secured a share of the spoils.

Winning just one of his past nine second-tier contests (D3 L5) in charge, Michael Skubala remains under severe pressure at Bristol City, who currently reside in an uninspiring 16th place in the table.

The Robins' sole victory in their current wretched run arrived on the road at Bolton on October 31, when Dom Ballard, Sam Bell and playmaker Scott Twine netted in a five-goal thriller.

Firing an attacking blank in five of their past eight matches ahead of Saturday's trip to The Hawthorns, there is no doubting that the Robins are failing to maximise the potential of Ballard and Lorent Tolaj, with the pair scoring 40 goals combined in League One last term.

After leading goalscorer Isaac Price missed the win at Bolton on Wednesday, West Brom boss Morrison revealed that the Northern Irishman is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks due to a knee injury.

The attacker joins midfielder Ousmane Diakite (calf) in the Albion treatment room, with the Mali international expected to be out until late December.

Right-back Noah Galves (knee) will not play again this season, whilst talented youngster Rabby Nzingoula is suspended for this weekend after collecting his fifth yellow card of the term at Bolton.

There was a serious injury scare for Bristol City on Tuesday night, when centre-back Luke McNally was forced off due to a knee issue.

The 27-year-old has previously missed nearly two years due to a problem with the same knee, meaning that Rob Dickie is likely to be drafted into the XI at The Hawthorns.

Sam Greenwood and Lisav Eissat were surprise omissions from the matchday squad last time out but could return to the fold on Saturday.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Campbell, Styles; Tunde, Horn Myhre, Molumby, Whitwell; Morgan, Heggebo

Collins; Tanner, Dickie, Atkinson, Pring; Wallace, Knight, Randell, Twine; Tolaj, Ballard

Aiming to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches, West Brom will be confident of beating Bristol City, even with Nzingoula, Price and Diakite all sidelined.

The Robins are certainly capable of producing a gutsy away performance but are likely to leave empty-handed on Saturday.

#2084. Le Havre vs. Strasbourg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09

Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.

The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.

Le Havre's 14th-placed finish last season, just three points above Nice in the relegation playoff spot, offered little encouragement ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and those concerns have proved justified.

Le Club Doyen have not won a top-flight fixture since beating Lorient 2-0 on the final day of last season, with their miserable start prompting Didier Digard's dismissal at the end of October.

Valerien Ismael's first match in charge of the basement club began brightly when Josh Maja scored after three minutes against Troyes; however, they held that advantage for just 15 minutes before eventually losing 3-1.

Conceding three more goals left Les Ciel et Marine with the competition's joint-worst defensive record, having shipped 25, while their tally of 10 scored surpasses only Angers' nine.

Even victory would do little to transform the Dean Club's position, as they enter this weekend eight points behind the relegation playoff spot and nine adrift of safety.

Nonetheless, the hosts must avoid defeat to Vitor Matos's Strasbourg, who occupy that playoff position.

Le Racing's disappointing start has already cost Hugo Oliveira his job, with Matos replacing his Portuguese compatriot during the international break.

The new manager's debut did not go to plan, with Le RCS losing 1-0 to Brest despite an encouraging performance in which they attempted 15 shots to their opponents' 16; Le Racing also created two chances deemed clear-cut to Brest's one.

Looking to build on that display, Le RCS target their fourth victory of the campaign this weekend, although it would be only their second since early October.

Maximum points could lift Matos's men out of the playoff spot and as high as 13th, although escaping the bottom three also requires Auxerre, Troyes or Le Mans to slip up.

The hosts have several absentees, with Felix Mambimbi (Achilles), Timothee Pembele (muscle), Rassoul Ndiaye (muscle), Daren Mosengo (ankle), Stephan Zagadou (ACL), Sota Nakamura (leg) and Lionel Mpasi (Achilles) all sidelined.

Enzo Koffi begins a two-match suspension following his late dismissal against Troyes last weekend, ruling him out of Saturday's encounter and December's trip to Lens.

Only six players have surpassed Maja's five league goals this season, but the Nigerian's efforts have brought little reward for a Dean Club side repeatedly undermined by defensive frailties.

Strasbourg have several potential game-changers, with Gessime Yassine registering four goals and three assists, Giovanni Reyna scoring three, Conrad Harder and Dario Essugo contributing two goals and an assist and Sebastian Nanasi setting up three.

However, Reyna is unavailable due to a muscle problem, while Fabio Balde (leg), Oso (knock) and Joaquin Panichelli (ACL) are also sidelined.

Bodart; Sasso, Seko, Touba; Ouziad, Mwanga, Ebonog, Richardson, Jelert; Maja, Fofana

Jorgensen; Antwi, Doukoure, Coulibaly, Hogsberg; Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Nanasi, Godo; Harder

Maja's scoring form offers Le Havre some encouragement, but conceding 25 goals in 11 matches suggests that their defensive problems remain too pronounced for an immediate recovery.

Strasbourg created enough chances to trouble Brest in Matos's first match and should find greater reward against the division's joint-leakiest defence.

#2083. “Thank goodness I scored” – Kessie admits he still sees Inter as a ‘derby’ game

Last night, AC Milan watched their former midfielder Franck Kessie help their top four chances and even their Scudetto hopes.

After a 5-1 win at San Siro, things couldn’t have got much better for Milan last night. Yet, somehow, they did. Indeed, the late kick-off on Sunday saw Atalanta host Inter and it seemed that the Nerazzurri were heading for another three points, having gone 4-2 up.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, a brace from Charles De Ketelaere – the second coming to make it 4-3 – and a late penalty from Kessie levelled the scoring and meant Inter stayed within two points of the Rossoneri.

Speaking to DAZN after his late equaliser, Kessie admitted that he still saw the game as a derby, even if he’s no longer a Rossoneri representative, as MilanPress relayed.

“We have great faith in coach Sarri and his staff. The season is still long. Tonight we responded strongly. A heavy penalty at the end? You can score or miss: it went well. For me, it was a small derby against Inter: thank goodness I scored… ”

Given what it means for the title race, the Diavolo will thank the Ivorian for his contribution and if he plays a part in another successful season, he’ll only be thanked more for it.

#2082. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#2081. How Ayden Heaven feels about leaving Manchester United as West Ham show interest in January deal

West Ham boss Scott Parker is determined to bolster his ranks in the winter transfer window. A striker and a left-back is on the WHUFC chief’s radar, and reports have said there is an interest in Manchester United’s Ayden Heaven too.

The 20-year-old could leave Old Trafford to find more game time, be it on loan or a permanent basis, and the Hammers are monitoring his situation. According to The Athletic, Heaven is keen to play more, but his true desire is to stay at Manchester United, fight for his place in the team and help their battle to rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

However, his need to play could force the issue and bring a January move to fruition. Premier League clubs have made contact to gauge Heaven’s availability and there may be a decision to make over his future in the coming weeks.

Heaven started his academy career in the West Ham setup, leaving in 2019 to join Arsenal. He cemented himself as one to watch while with Arsenal, but a desire to find more first-team opportunities prompted a move to Manchester United in the winter of 2025.

He broke into the side under Ruben Amorim but has primarily played as a backup since. The London-born prospect is held in very high regard, but the need for immediate results at Manchester United means new boss Mauricio Pochettino would be taking a gamble in entrusting Heaven with a starting berth.

As a left-footed centre-back, Heaven is adept at progressing the ball from deep with a good passing ability and a willingness to carry the ball in dribbles. This aspect of his game was nurtured at Arsenal, and it has helped him slot in at Old Trafford.

He deals with aerial duels well for a player of his inexperience, but his limited senior game time has seen issues regarding anticipation and one-on-one defending arise. Heaven can develop in these scenarios over time though – he just needs regular exposure at first-team level.

A drop to the Championship could benefit Heaven. He would be backed to start regularly at West Ham, likely taking Max Kilman’s place to slot in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos at centre-back.

Playing in a team that wants to challenge for promotion and play possession football would make for good exposure for Heaven. However, it would not be a surprise if his sights are set higher.

Heaven is a highly-rated prospect who has already played Premier League football, and he will be confident in his belief that he can deliver at top-flight level if entrusted with a regular role. It could make clubs in higher leagues more attractive than WHUFC, especially on a permanent basis.

The Hammers should keep track on his situation, but be aware that they could be outdone if the door does open for Heaven to move on from Old Trafford.

#2080. Not a forward: Why Mikel Arteta may need to bolster surprise Arsenal position amid January twist

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier currently providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:18, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:45

Andoni Iraola's side start the next batch of fixtures sitting in fourth position in the Premier League table.

Possible return date: December 2 (vs. Sunderland)

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

Wolves travel to Lincoln City this weekend looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine games after thumping Derby County 3-0 on Tuesday. Adam Armstrong struck twice against the Rams, while Mateus Mane continued his impressive recent form by opening his account for the season.

Ahead of the trip to Lincoln, Cesar Peixoto has provided the injury latest for his squad. As reported by Inside Wolves, Peixoto was positive about his squad situation, and even revealed how Raul Jimenez is progressing.

“Raul came yesterday to see the doctor, the specialist, and the recuperation is going very, very well; that’s what the specialist said,” Peixoto said. “I don’t know if the medical department lets me say this, but it’s true! I think it’s not a problem.

#2075. Stevenage vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:55

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

Revell will, however, remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts, who are all still sidelined through injury.

For what is likely to be Thompson's third and final match in charge of Blackpool, the former midfielder will once again be without several first-team players.

A sickness bug kept Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe out of recent matches, but all three returned for the clash with the Foxes and are expected to feature again this weekend.

Dale Taylor, defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe, as well as captain George Honeyman, are all likely to remain unavailable for the trip to Hertfordshire.

Having scored his second goal of the season after coming off the bench last time out, Ennis is likely to be rewarded with a starting place and could replace either Dion Charles or Jerry Yates.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Phillips, Thompson; Sanderson, Broggio, Patterson; Magennis

Peacock-Farrell; Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Munroe; Niskanen, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Ennis, Charles

With one of the best defensive sides in the English Football League meeting a team who have struggled to score on a regular basis, we expect Boro to edge a low-scoring contest.

We expect the Seasiders' struggles to continue with Boro making it four unbeaten in the league and closing out November with a sixth win of the season.

#2074. The 9 players set to miss QPR vs Sheffield United ft 53-cap international defender

Sheffield United laid down their promotion credentials in their midweek draw against Southampton, and now travel to the capital to take on another top eight side in QPR.

The Blades had gotten to the periphery of the play-offs on a rather favourable run of fixtures. With Southampton, QPR, West Brom and Middlesbrough to play between last Tuesday and Boxing Day, we were going to find out a lot about how serious this side is.

And while it may only be one game in that run of four against sides in the top eight, their performance for the final hour against the Saints was very impressive, and while their equaliser didn't come until the 90th minute, they were good value for that, and maybe even more.

Now they have to back that up and take on a QPR side who have been one of the more well-organised outfits in the division so far this season. The Hoops have the third-best overall xGA, the best from set pieces, and have faced the fourth-fewest shots.

Julien Stephan's side look more and more like promotion contenders as the season goes on, and they have a chance to go five points clear of one of their nearest challengers. It's a big matchup at Loftus Road, but these nine players won't be available for it.

The most recent doubt about QPR concerns versatile attacker Paul Smyth, who was withdrawn from the squad on Tuesday against Norwich City due to an upset stomach.

It's a quick turnaround, but we'll see if the Northern Irishman will be fit enough to go again against Sheffield United.

Club captain Jimmy Dunne has missed the last two games after picking up an ankle injury while on international duty with the Republic of Ireland.

Speaking ahead of the draw against Norwich, Julien Stephan stated that his injury wasn't a bad one, but conceded that he didn't know when he'd be fit enough to return to action.

There is a definitive timeline on Alfie Lloyd's hamstring injury, though, with it being revealed at the start of the month that the striker will be out for the rest of the calendar year.

Lloyd hasn't been able to get any consistency in the R's side so far this season, with a couple of setbacks coming after he netted his first goal of the campaign in a 4-1 win over Derby County last month.

#2067. Exclusive: Fresh Robbie Fowler to Swindon Town update revealed after Ian Holloway sack

Swindon Town are on the search for a new manager, with Ian Holloway's time at the County Ground coming to an end earlier in the week.

The 63-year-old had been in charge of the Robins for the past two years, having endured a storied career which has taken him to the Premier League with both Blackpool and Crystal Palace.

Improvement was showed in both seasons finished by Holloway, with 12th and ninth-placed finishes in League Two, but results have been indifferent during the current campaign, with back-to-back defeats over Grimsby Town and Newport County leading to his dismissal.

Swindon's hierarchy - which includes chairman Clem Morfuni - must now find Holloway's successor, and FLW can exclusively reveal that one individual who is on the radar is none other than Premier League legend Robbie Fowler.

Fowler scored 163 Premier League goals in his career for Liverpool, Leeds United and Manchester City, whilst also appearing 26 times for the England national team, before winding down his career in Australia and Thailand.

We looked at five potential replacements Swindon Town should consider if they part company with under-pressure manager Ian Holloway.

Since his retirement, Fowler has been well-travelled as a manager, with spells in both Thailand and Australia, as well as India and Saudi Arabia, but he's yet to land a job in his native England, having been without a role since being with Al-Qadsiah in 2023.

That could now change though, with Football League World understanding that the 51-year-old is a live contender to become the latest person to have a go at the Town job.

One of the reasons that Fowler is being admired by Swindon chairman Morfuni is his time in his native Australia, FLW can reveal.

After a spell at Blackburn Rovers, Fowler moved down under in 2009 to play for North Queensland Fury, a stint which lasted a year before moving on to fellow Aussie club Perth Glory.

Fowler would join Muangthong United in Thailand in 2011 and end up becoming their player-manager for a short period of time, but some eight years after leaving Australia, the former striker would return as a manager, taking the Brisbane Roar job.

Managing 23 games for the Queensland-based outfit, Fowler won 11 times as their manager, before the A-League was suspended in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic - he wouldn't return to the club as he relocated to be closer to his family.

A further 20 matches were managed for East Bengal between 2020 and 2021, before a stint in Saudi with Al-Qadsiah lasted just three months, despite winning six of his eight matches in charge and going unbeaten in the Saudi second tier, with the club wanting to move to a more Spanish-style model, according to Fowler himself.
