#2055. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”

Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

We were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

Overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a big credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

We know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

It was my best [performance for Newcastle] so far. New manager, new role. I’m so pleased to be here. I hope today I showed I’m really happy.

It’s rough, especially 30 seconds before the end of the game, but that’s a huge step for us. That’s the mentality we need to have through the season. The manager came three weeks ago and gave us a lot of information. Now we show on the pitch we are ready for the season. We needed this win to make a statement but in the end we draw. We have so much to work on.

To be honest, I didn’t even hear the referee’s whistle. I had to look at him if I can go. I was practising a lot during the pre-season. We didn’t have any penalties during games, but in training. We need to take the positivity of the first game and move on.

More than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - new but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

If I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.

🗣️ "It's knee on knee, it's a foul"Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge analyse Lewis Hall's foul which led to Liverpool's late penalty. pic.twitter.com/NRw406sTcZ

14 - Liverpool remain unbeaten on MD1 in the Premier League in each of the last 14 seasons (since 2013-14), the longest active run in the competition.Spirited. pic.twitter.com/3rluUnSBhu

I think they did the right thing, easy to say now of course, by not giving Isak the penalty. There is enough pressure on in the 96th minute without all that would have entailed. Nor was Isak having the best of games.

A familiar feeling after last season. Newcastle concede a last kick of the game penalty. Should have held on for the win. It was a soft penalty, Hall dangled out a knee rather than a leg and Munoz made sure he ran into it. But as soon as it's given on the field never going to be…

The points are shared, and Lewis Hall has his hands on his knees. Jaissle protests with the officials. This was a stirring home performance from Newcastle which should build confidence for the season ahead. An irrepressible showing from Wissa was the biggest positive. Iraola will be pleased to get back on the coach with a draw after what was quite a ragged Liverpool performance, their midfield balance looked off.

What a magnificent penalty from Szoboszlai, Hornicek had no chance, and Liverpool have surely snatched a point.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

What theatre that would be... Gakpo has the ball in his hands. But no, it’s going to be Szoboszlai.

With the last kick of the game, practically. Kerkez launched the ball forward, Van Dijk competed for a header, Munoz pounced on the seconds, and his pace carried enough threat to prompt Hall to step across the winger and make contact with his knee.

#NEWLIV – 90+6' The referee's call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR. REF: "He doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact". VAR: "It's knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty".

So, so poor from Frimpong who hesitates to put a cross in, takes a couple of unconvincing touches, and then commits a foul. Mac Allister. Wissa receives a standing ovation, replaced by Schar.

Gakpo runs down a blind alley, and it is another blunt Liverpool attack. Time running out for them now.

Liverpool corner, won by Lewis Koumas who lacked support but his cross deflects behind.

Hornicek palms away Szoboszlai’s delivery. This has been strong Premier League debut from the goalkeeper.

Newcastle have a throw deep in Liverpool territory after more good work from Wissa, and chaotic defending from Liverpool. Atwell has booked Gakpo for an earlier foul on Wissa.

There will be FIVE minutes of added time.

Murphy with another wonderful cross through the Liverpool six-yard box, but no player in black and white was gambling for a tap in. Liverpool just about still in with a sniff.

Cheers at St James’ Park as Thiaw ushers the ball behind as Kerkez tried to get in behind. Then Frimpong’s touch lets him down, not for the first time.

An aimless cross from Liverpool, and Munoz is penalised at the back post for a push. Liverpool have lacked clarity and intelligence in the last third today, but there is still time.

Big save by Alisson! He narrows the angle to deny Wissa the goal his performance deserves. How important could that prove to be? Liverpool have the ball again.

Liverpool with a long spell of possession in the final third, trying to tire Newcastle legs, but Frimpong’s cross is a little too high for Isak to generate any power with the header. Newcastle are just starting to sit in a touch.

Munoz runs down a blind alley, more sound defending from Lewis Hall and the Newcastle players can see the finish line now. They will be only too aware of how they lost this game in the last minute 12 months ago, though.

Szoboszlai shoots against the well, and the Araujo is booked for bundling over a Newcastle defender. Wissa thought he was away for Newcastle but the flag goes up for offside.

Frimpong does well to keep things alive for Liverpool, and there are half-hearted appeals for a handball penalty but Thiaw was down by his side. Another Liverpool sub: Lewis Koumas is on for Gravenberch.

The long throw is headed away, but Murphy catches Mac Allister and Liverpool have a free-kick in a crossing position. Though you never can tell with Szoboszlai around.

Here come those changes from Newcastle: Murphy and Bamba on for Elanga and Miley. Hall’s delivery from the free-kick won by Wissa was poor.

Liverpool have Newcastle penned in, but Munoz’s pass is overhit and Newcastle have a goal kick. Jaissle is about to introduce Jacob Murphy from the bench. Wissa, Newcastle’s best player by a stretch, does well to win a free-kick high up the pitch from Szoboszlai.

Araujo is on for Jacquet at the back for Liverpool, who have just threatened again. Szoboszlai hacked down but the referee waved play on, and Kerkez could not get enough curl on his cross or else Isak would have had a free header.

Willock lifts in a teasing cross from the right, Alisson palms the ball back into danger, and Ramsey cracks a shot wide of the post. Hard to say whether this game is going 3-1 or 2-2 but the scoring is surely not over.

Was that Isak’s moment? Gakpo rolls the ball back to Isak in a good shooting position just inside the box, but he slices his left-footed effort well over the bar. More cheers from the Newcastle fans.

Newcastle really should have three! Defence-splitting pass from Miley to release Hall, who feeds a teasing cross into the six-yard box, but Wissa could only get studs on it. Better connection and that was a goal. Liverpool so fragile at the back, though.

Stuart Atwell has been guessing on decisions throughout this game, and Jacob Ramsey has just been booked for what looked a clean challenge on Isak, who produced a lovely turn initially. Newcastle survive the free-kick.

But then Gakpo has acres of space to run into, but Botman saves the day in the box. The game is haywire at the moment.

Here come the Liverpool changes: Ngumoha, who was the match-winner last season here, Wirtz are the players off, replaced by Munoz and Mac Allister.

Liverpool will be kicking themselves, they had Newcastle on the ropes. Iraola is preparing a triple sub. Willock was the goalscorer, but it was also a brilliant assist from Wissa.

The equaliser had been coming but that was really poor from a defensive perspective as everyone backed off Cody Gakpo and let him pick his spot.

You also have to question the decision to keep Will Osula on. He was obviously struggling to move freely and it has meant Newcastle did not have an out ball.

But, just as I was going to be critical of manager Matthias Jassile one of his substitutes puts Newcastle back in front and it a brilliant goal. Magnificent build up play from Wissa, who skipped away from three Liverpool players, but it is even better from Joe Willock who takes the pass in his stride, shows great skill t o take it on jis stride and away from Frimpong and the finish is sublime, curled into the bottom corner.

Jaissle can claim that as a magical substitution, but it is superb individual goal from Joe Willock. Another Newcastle counter-attack, Wissa does brilliantly to wriggle away from three players in midfield, and Willock dribbles inside Frimpong before arcing a shot into the far corner. Outstanding finish.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

Jaissle with a double sub immediately after conceding: Joe Willock and Jacob Ramsey are on, replacing William Osula and Sean Steur who was a little slack on the Gakpo goal.

The game is one-way traffic, Liverpool looking to turn the screw.

The man linked with a move to Spurs all summer has equalised for Liverpool. He had a sighter a few minutes earlier, and it was too easy for Gakpo to receive the ball behind Newcastle’s midfield, and he had time to pick out the far corner with a clean hit from outside the box. Game on.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

Just two touches inside the Newcastle penalty area from Isak so far, he has been subdued. Nice idea from Gakpo, chopping inside from the left, and curling a shot not far wide of the top corner.

Good defending from Lewis Hall up against Ngumoha, before Van Dijk passes the ball straight of play. Wissa wanted a free-kick for a challenge from behind by Gravenberch but the referee judged he touched the ball first.

Scramble at the back post from the Liverpool corner, but then a loose touch from Wirtz prompts a Newcastle break and there was a chance for Elanga to dribble into the box but he put the breaks on.

The game is already really stretched, holes appearing in Liverpool’s midfield. Wissa’s poked through ball towards Osula was just a tad overhit.

Liverpool have made a sharp start from kick off, winning a corner.

Just because it is a manager’s first game, we shouldn’t pull our punches. That was a scandalous first half performance from Liverpool and there is absolutely no difference in watching them now compared to what they offered through much of last season. Maybe the disappointment wasn’t about the man in the dugout. Maybe it was about the players wearing the Red shirt.

5 & 18 - 5 - Liverpool have conceded in the opening five minutes on MD1 of a Premier League season for the very first time.The Reds are winless in 18 Premier League away games when falling 1-0 behind (D6 L12) since beating Crystal Palace 2-1 in December 2023.Baptism. pic.twitter.com/K1HF2wNRVP

Newcastle will be delighted to go in leading the game at half time but there were some worrying signs before the break.

They had stopped getting up the pitch and were invited a lot of pressure from Liverpool. Will Osula has clearly picked up an injury – he took a whack on his achilles midway through the half – and will surely need to be replaced by Nick Woltemade in the second half with Yoane Wissa moving up top.

Alexander Isak has been on the receiving end of a number of heavy tackles and has looked pretty miserable so far on his return to St James’ Park.

But Liverpool are not going to keep getting into dangerous positions and fail to capitalise on them. Things for Matthias Jaissle to sort out before the second half.

LFC Midfield all bombing forward happened all pre season, madness!

Plenty of possession for Liverpool, but not enough cutting edge of crispness in their play in the final third. On top of that problem, they were vulnerable to Newcastle’s pace and direct play early on although that threat abated as the half progressed. Jaissle will be delighted with the commitment and application of his players, but Osula may have to come off with a knock.

Isak hooks a pass towards Frimpong straight out of play, causing much mirth among the home fans.

Foul given against Wissa on Gravenberch, and the Newcastle forward needs to be careful on a yellow. I’m not sure there was any contact at all. Wissa drags a shot across the face of Liverpool’s goal and wide.

Gravenberch with a speculative shot which is blocked, before Dedic blasts the ball off Gakpo to win a goal kick. Dan Burn is watching on from the stands, Newcastle’s new club captain who is absent because of a rolled ankle. Also up there in the gods is England manager Thomas Tuchel.

Much better cross from Frimpong, but Dedic clears at the back post for a Liverpool corner. Danger as Gakpo flicks the ball on at the neat post, and the ball bounces off Botman and behind for another corner. Gravenberch tries a cute reverse pass towards Isak, but it deflects through to Hornicek. Isak has been ever so quiet.

William Osula is hobbling up top for Newcastle, which is a worry because has been a menace so far. The same can be said of Yoane Wissa who is having a stormer as a second striker, dropping into midfield at times.

Stuart Atwell being a little card happy, now Lewis Miley is shown a yellow for a foul on Gravenberch. Just looked a regulation midfield foul, not sure a booking was necessary.

Osula took the free-kick, straight into the wall, but his follow up effort deflects off Szoboszlai and behind for a corner. Excellent delivery from Lewis Hall, cleared by Van Dijk.

Wirtz and Isak do well down the left to start a Liverpool counter with runners forward, but Frimpong’s delivery from the right is atrocious.

Liverpool starting to monopolise possession, without a crafty final pass. Kerkez has been booked for holding Elanga, who is giving him a going over on Newcastle’s right flank.

Then Barnes rolls inside Frimpong and drives inside, and the Liverpool right-back is booked for a challenge from behind. May well have been a harsh call, both plays were grasping for a piece of shirt.

Both of Liverpool’s full-backs on yellows now.

Wissa booked for a mistimed challenge, and Liverpool have a free-kick 30 yards out. Szoboszlai is thinking about a shot... but he blasts his shot straight into the wall.

Osula then does very well to make it stick and drag Newcastle up the pitch but the move fizzles out.

It’s an experience in itself watching Andoni Iraola on the sideline. He’s going to have clocked up 10,000 steps for sure by the final whistle and his increasing animation is indicative of Liverpool’s anaemic start. You would expect Liverpool to score at some point but this is a team that has lots of questions to answer.

Isak down on the turf after a strong challenge by Lewis Hall, no foul given much to the delight of the Newcastle fans.

Then the home team cut through Liverpool again, Wissa with a glorious outside of the foot pass behind Jacquet for the run of Osula, but the Liverpool defender just about got a toe to the ball as the striker closed in on Alisson. Great challenge in the end from the wrong side.

Nice counter-movement between Elanga and Dedic the right-back. Elanga faked to drop inside, taking Kerkez and Gakpo with him, and Miley’s switch found Dedic on the outside. Cross is blocked, and Newcastle have a corner. Cleared, and then a poor Szoboszlai pass is blocked when there was a chance to release Wirtz on the counter.

It feels like all the 50:50s are dropping Newcastle’s way at the moment. It has been a very energetic start, the question is whether that is sustainable across the game so early in the season. The tempo will surely drop at some point.

Peter Beardsley, Tino Asprilla and Shaka Hislop among Keegan’s former players watching on.

Hornicek with his first big save of the game, tipping Wirtz’s shot around the post. Newcastle failed to deal with a Kerkez cross and the ball dropped to the German for a snap shot. Newcastle defend the corner.

“There’s only one greedy b-----d,” is the chant from the Newcastle fans (aimed at Isak, for the uninitiated).

Wissa goes down looking for a foul but nothing doing, but there are cheers from the home fans as Isak is beaten to a header and then Sean Steur turns away from pressure well in midfield. There is more bite about the home team in the challenges than Liverpool, Jaissle will be delighted with this.

Echoes of last season with Liverpool’s defence looking suspect against direct play, Alisson with an unconvincing intervention outside his penalty area after the ball held up. He is fortunate that Wissa did not connect with the volley when there was a chance to lob the goalkeeper.

What a difference a year makes. Anthony Elanga was played in on goal against Aston Villa on his Premier League debut for Newcastle United 12 months ago. He looked nervous and hit a tame effort too close to the goalkeeper.

It is fair to say that was a sign of things to come for the winger who endured a miserable first season on Tyneside following a high-profile £55m move from Nottingham Forest. He looked drained of confidence and lacked the composure and technical ability to succeed in black and white stripes.

Fast forward 12 months and he has just taken a very similar chance against Liverpool. The speed of Will Osula sent the visiting defence into retreat, and his pace and excellent first touch set up the chance, which he finished clinically.

That was the player Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer. It was the player Newcastle supporters thought was going to offer a major upgrade in the right wing position.

If Elanga has a better season this time around it will be a huge boost to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

Elanga vs Kerkez is a match-up which looks advantageous for Newcastle, the Liverpool left-back is at full tilt to get back and by a foul after a lofted Wissa pass over his head towards the rapid Sweden winger.

This is a very open game already, and Liverpool are back on the front foot. Szoboszlai whips in a free-kick which appears to glance of Van Dijk’s head, but the referee awards a corner. Hall clears, but Newcastle do not clear their lines and Gakpo’s shot is blocked by Thiaw.

Liverpool caught out on the break, but it is a really well-executed goal from Newcastle’s perspective. Gravenberch should have let fly at the other end, but after the move broke down Osula was able to receive in space and turn to face Van Dijk and Jacquet. He waited for the support of Elanga to arrive, and he burned down the outside of Kerkez. Well-weighted pass put him through, and the finish across Alisson was ideal.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

Lewis Hall wins a challenge at the edge of the box which receives a roar of approval from the crowd, but Liverpool quickly settle into a long spell of possession, with Gravenberch turning away from pressure, but neglecting to shoot.

This already has the feel of a very helter-skelter game. Newcastle won a free-kick inside 20 seconds, clipped into the penalty area but it was claimed by Alisson. Then a Liverpool attack swept from one end to the other with Wirtz’s shot blocked at the edge of the box. This should be tasty.

That roar turns to vociferous boos as Alexander Isak takes the kick-off.

They would have still been clapping until tomorrow if the whistle hadn’t been blown by referee Stuart Attwell to start the game but the flip from adulation for Kevin Keegan to absolute vitriol towards Alexander Isak was incredible. 50,000 in black and white are singing a song aimed at him. The only two words we can get away with printing are “ole, ole!” - use your imagination for what might have preceded it!

A period of applause for Kevin Keegan at St James' Park 👏❤️ pic.twitter.com/AsSGOkpVPN

There is a minute’s applause for Keegan, which ends with a defending roar.

Liverpool have just taken to the field for their warm up, predictably to a back drop of pantomime booing. But there is a nice touch from the club, as each member of Andoni Iraola’s squad is wearing a jersey with “Keegan 7” on the back. It’s going to be a day of heavy emotion.

Alan Shearer was one of those fans holding up a white card:

The Keegan quote on the Newcastle banner is: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should, we should all be dreamers at heart. Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that’, but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well, I say, ‘Why not?’”

Banners are being unfurled in the Gallowgate End. Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce are in the stands, and Les Ferdinand is pitchside speaking on Sky.

As you know it’s a transition phase and a huge challenge. There will be some activity in the transfer market new week, hopefully, but we go for it, we are as ready as we can be. That’s something we want to show the fans, we want to go all in.

As soon as I saw him on the pitch, I was falling in love. He is a great guy with great potential.

I’m not worried. As a manager, a player or a squad, if it is against you you want to play this kind of games.

Difficult call, Jeremy has very good skills with the ball, without the ball they will be very demanding today, playing against Wissa and Osula.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

He could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

It is sad in many ways and shows the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Frimpong, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak

The Reds to take on Newcastle in our season opener ✊ #NEWLIV

Barnes, Wissa, Osula and Elanga start in what could be a front four. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur, just 20 and 18 respectively, will need to get through an immense amount of work in midfield.

Newcastle United XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Miley, Steur; Elanga, Wissa, Barnes; Osula

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Bobby Moncur are the representatives of both clubs with wreaths, and Shola Ameobi is behind Dalglish. Ian Rush is also in attendance, who spent one season on Tyneside in the twilight of his career when Dalglish was the manager.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. That will surely sting Liverpool fans more than most, given the city’s strong sense of regional identity. You can read more on the subject in this article by Dominic King. Trent on loan in January, anyone?

He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

#2054. “I honestly didn’t expect it” – Journalist claims Milan have made €70m offer for Endrick

It seems AC Milan have made an offer for Endrick in recent days, with a Spanish journalist shocked at the situation.

Talk of Endrick arriving at San Siro is dominating the news, and it’s clear that Milan are not messing around here. Indeed, they are looking to beat off interest from other European clubs and they may well be close to doing so.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Jose Mourinho is still opposing a deal, but the Brazilian’s entourage was in Italy last week and it seems that a move to San Siro is becoming less of a hypothetical and more of a tangible possibility.

Speaking to SER Radio, Anton Meana looked at the reporting from Italy about the Rossoneri’s interest in Endrick and how the situation was actually unfolding.

“AC Milan’s offer is formal and they want to sign him in January. The Rossoneri have already informed the player, and if he can’t leave in January, they’ll see about negotiations in the summer. But AC Milan’s firm offer is now on the table.

“The owner of AC Milan wants to offer close to 70 million euros to sign Endrick now. The problem is that Mourinho prefers to keep him because he knows there wouldn’t be a signing that could match or surpass the Brazilian.

“It’s good for him to have Endrick because he’s good, because he provides competition for Mbappé, and because he trains hard for every match. I want to see how the next few weeks unfold. I’d say Endrick isn’t going to leave, but the player’s entourage, his agents, will be in Madrid this week or early next week seeking talks and exploring the striker’s immediate future.

“I thought it was just the typical bluff from the Italian transfer press, who constantly promote players and see them as being in Serie A all the time, but this offer from Milan, I honestly didn’t expect it. The interest, as Cerruti told you, is very serious, and if they can, they want to sign Endrick this winter transfer window.”

It’s safe to say that the Diavolo’s interest is more than speculative and with an official offer on the table, things may begin to move between Milan and Madrid.

#2053. Real Madrid vs. Alaves: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:18

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday evening.

Los Blancos will enter the league fixture off the back of a thumping 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho's side have now won each of their last 10 matches in all competitions, including their last six fixtures in Spain's top flight.

Real Madrid beat Celta Vigo 2-1 in the league last time out, and they currently sit second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona.

Alaves, meanwhile, have been one of the success stories in La Liga this season, picking up 16 points from 13 matches, which has left them in ninth spot in the table.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up the head-to-head record and looks at the previous meetings between the two teams ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital.

Real Madrid have tackled Alaves on 46 occasions throughout history, and unsurprisingly, the Madrid giants lead the overall head-to-head record with 38 wins to Alaves five, while there have only ever been three draws between the two teams.

Karim Benzema is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored nine times against Alaves during his time at Real Madrid.

Real Madrid are on 121 goals against Alaves, conceding just 34, and Los Blancos are on a nine-game winning run against the Basque side.

That said, Alaves do have a recent famous win over Real Madrid to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory when the two teams locked horns at Bernabeu in November 2020, thanks to goals from Lucas Perez and Joselu.

Alaves have beaten Real Madrid only twice since 2000, though, while there has not been a draw between the two sides since October 2001.

Two of Alaves' five wins over Los Blancos have actually come at the Bernabeu, also triumphing 1-0 in the famous stadium back in 2000.

In La Liga, the teams have met on 40 occasions, with Real Madrid winning 34 times to Alaves' four, drawing twice in the process.

#2052. Lincoln City warned against repeating Michael Skubala 'experiment' with Gavin Strachan

Lincoln City are on the hunt for a new head coach after parting company with Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw earlier this week.

Lincoln won the League One title last season to secure a return to the second tier of English football for the first time in 65 years, but just weeks after sealing promotion, they lost head coach Michael Skubala to Bristol City, with Cohen and Shaw stepping up to replace him.

It is fair to say that Lincoln's decision to appoint Cohen and Shaw as joint-head coaches raised a few eyebrows, and they were widely tipped for relegation at the start of the season, but the pair made an impressive start to life in the Sincil Bank dugout.

After losing their opening two games, the Imps went on a five-game unbeaten run which lifted them to as high as eighth in the Championship table in mid-September, but results have declined significantly in recent months.

Lincoln have won just one of their last 10 games, and after suffering their fifth consecutive defeat as they were hammered 4-0 at Charlton Athletic on Tuesday night, Cohen and Shaw were dismissed on Wednesday morning with the club sitting 21st, just three points clear of the relegation zone.

There has been a shortage of rumours about potential successors to Cohen and Shaw so far, but journalist Alan Nixon reported on Thursday that West Bromwich Albion coach Gavin Strachan is one name under consideration by the Imps.

Strachan has plenty of coaching experience under his belt, having previously worked at the likes of Peterborough United, Doncaster Rovers and Celtic, and he has been part of James Morrison's backroom staff at The Hawthorns since the summer, but his only managerial experience is a brief four-and-a-half month spell with seventh tier side Ilkeston in 2015.

When asked for his thoughts on the possible appointment of Strachan, FLW's Lincoln City fan pundit Gary Hutchinson insisted that the Imps cannot afford to take a risk like they did with Skubala in League One, and he urged the club to bring in a manager with Championship experience.

"I think Gavin Strachan would be too much of a gamble for the club," Gary told FLW.

"I think they're looking for somebody with managerial experience.

"We're not in the same position as when we appointed Michael Skubala.

"When we were in League One, even though we were a smaller fish, there were always six or seven teams below us with smaller budgets, so we were expected not to be in the bottom four.

"The bottom four was failure, so we could afford to experiment a little bit, and that was the case with Michael Skubala.

"I think this calls for the same sort of thing as we had in the National League, get a manager in who understands the division a little bit more and who perhaps has experience of handling players and picking players up because they're going to need that.

"That performance on Tuesday night was not good enough.

"Whilst Gavin Strachan may well be a very good coach, we've had two coaches at the helm, and I think we need somebody who's got experience of the top job, as well as the coaching credentials.

"Bear in mind, on the coaching field, we've got Paul McShane and Shaun Pearson, who are both very competent coaches, so we need a figurehead to pull that back in.

"I just think, with Gavin Strachan, his lack of actual managerial experience will hold him back."

Who has the best and worst average attendances in the Championship so far this season? Football League World takes a look...

Lincoln have often taken gambles with their managerial decisions over the years, and they were certainly rewarded for the bold appointment of Skubala, whose only senior dugout experience prior to his arrival at Sincil Bank was a few games as caretaker of Leeds United in the Premier League.

However, the failed Cohen and Shaw experiment underlines the dangers of such risks in the Championship, and while the duo's time in charge should not be remembered as a disaster given that the Imps are currently outside the relegation zone, they should learn lessons and make a safer choice on this occasion.

Who should Lincoln City target to replace Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw? Tell us in the comments below!

Strachan is clearly a talented coach who has enjoyed plenty of success during his career, including helping Celtic to five consecutive Scottish Premiership titles, and he has made a big impact at West Brom this season, but he would not be the right man for Lincoln at this time.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2051. Torino vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23

Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.

Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, Lazio sit three points above reigning champions Inter and two clear of city rivals Roma after storming through their first dozen games.

Having begun Gennaro Gattuso's reign with a shock Coppa Italia loss to Mantova, the Biancocelesti have since gone up through the gears, only dropping four points in Serie A so far.

Victory this week would take them onto 11 wins from 13 games, and the last team to make such a fast start was Napoli in the 2022-23 campaign, when they ultimately went on to win the title.

Lazio's most recent success, against Lecce, featured goals from two of their star players this term, as Tijjani Noslin bagged a brace before Davide Frattesi capped things off with a cheeky chip from outside the box.

Ahead of next month's Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could well be at stake, fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

However, Gattuso will not look any further than Saturday's trip north to Turin, where Lazio have won half of their last 22 Serie A games against Torino.

That said, the capital club did not prevail when they last met in March, as Torino won 2-0 at Stadio Olimpico Grande.

So, the hosts can now seek back-to-back victories over Lazio for the first time since 2013, even if current form suggests they may fail.

While their Roman rivals are flying high, Toro have endured an uneven season under new boss Ignazio Abate: following a slow start, they then posted three consecutive wins, before slipping back down the table.

After last week's 1-0 loss to Napoli, Abate's side have picked up just one point from their last four matches, leaving them closer to the drop zone than Italy's top six.

While leaving Naples with anything is always a tough task, they cannot expect to thrive when they return to Turin.

Not only have the Granata conceded an average of nearly two goals per game there this season, but they are also on a record run of 11 Serie A home games without a clean sheet.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has generally stuck to a similar Lazio lineup, but he is currently missing two regular starters.

Though defensive duo Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo are both sidelined with flexor injuries, captain Mattia Zaccagni has resumed full training and could be named on the bench.

While Frattesi is the visitors' top scorer with five Serie A goals, Noslin has notched at least one goal involvement in all of his last four matches.

Torino have been less potent this term, but Che Adams has four top-flight strikes and Giovanni Simeone must love playing his father's old club - the Argentinian has previously scored 10 league goals against Lazio.

Ardian Ismajli limped out of the loss to Napoli with an adductor injury and has subsequently undergone surgery, while Abate has fitness doubts about wing-backs Rafik Belghali and Ricardo Rodriguez.

As Belghali is still suffering with knee inflammation, Zakaria Aboukhlal, Nicolo Fortini or even Nathan Patterson could fill in on the hosts' right flank.

Perri; Comuzzo, Coco, Comert; Aboukhlal, Braganca, Mandragora, Vlasic, Cacciamani; Adams, Simeone

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Well acquainted from their Milan days, Gattuso and Abate will be foes for 90 minutes this weekend, when Lazio should continue their long unbeaten run.

As Torino struggle to keep clean sheets, the league leaders are sure to score, and they have conceded under one goal per game so far this term.

#2050. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Also, it was Pulisics’ pass to Moreira that set-up Cisse’s goal. If were recognizing “hockey assists” then Pulisic’s pass to Moreira was also world-class. Not to be a wet-blanket, but Moreira and Cisse need to develop composure on the ball. Too often Moreira would negate his speed on the ball by dribbling into multiple defenders without looking to pass to an open teammate. Against the top teams Milan will not have as many goal scoring opportunities as they did on Sunday so now is the time to work on finding the open man in the final third.

So young players with potential, need to learn to be better and realise thier potential.

It was a pass in a 3v3 counter-attack situation. Great pass but Modric took out 5 defenders with 1 move. That is why it is world class and Pulisic pass is not mentioned as much.

Did anyone notice how Pulisic slowed down his run, thus letting Ramos reach the penalty box earlier and score his long awaited goal? Such a team player..

He’s always been that guy. Sometimes I wish he can be more ‘selfish’. Another example is the penalty fiasco with Tammy back then.

Yes. I’d say it was as much about letting Ramos score as it was about “arriving” in the box late, setting up a cut back score, which he learned from Frank Lampard. Both are good things.

#2049. Top 20 most valuable EFL League One strikers right now

Strikers are where the big money lies, and every club across the EFL wants their line-leaders to have high value.

In League One, that's no different, and with the third tier looking the tightest it's been in quite some time this season, a good number nine could end up being the difference between staying up or going down, mid-table or the play-offs, or maybe even going up automatically.

We saw last season how Leyton Orient's third-tier status was heavily preserved by Dom Ballard's goals and how the excellence of Bim Pepple and Lorent Tolaj drove a once hapless Plymouth Argyle side up the division in the second half of the season.

Two of those went for big money to Bristol City this past summer, but which current League One strikers could do the same?

According to Transfermarkt's data, these are the 20 strikers with the most value in the third tier right now.

N.B. All values are initially in Euros - converted to Pounds for the list

MK Dons re-signed Sam Nombe this past summer from Rotherham United for a guaranteed £600,000, which could surpass £1 million if add-ons are met.

The 28-year-old was bought when the Millers were in the Championship off the back of a 15-goal season with Exeter City, and then would score 14 and 12 in the last two seasons at the level in South Yorkshire, albeit last year ending in relegation.

That would have dropped his value, per Tranfsermarkt's ranks, but you'd expect another 10-goal season at least in this free-scoring MK side.

It's been a difficult few years for Gassan Ahadme. His value would have been sky-high after being signed for Charlton Athletic off the back of 11 goals in 29 third tier games for Cambridge United in 2023/24.

But, a couple of dud years, whether that be at the Valley in their promotion campaign, or last season at Stevenage, have lowered that back down, and now he's back at the Abbey, already with more league goals than he's managed in his last two seasons combined.

Bosnian frontman Admir Bristric was an intriguing signing for Leicester City to make this past summer. The 23-year-old scored 15 in 29 in all competitions last season for Slovenian side NK Bravo, and the Foxes paid at least €1.15m (£963k) for his services.

Unfortunately, Emil Riis signed less than a month later, and all of a sudden, Bristric was relegated to cameo roles and was quickly shunned out of League One plans.

His only appearances in the last three months have been in the EFL Trophy and the FA Cup against National League North side Oxford City. Even then, he only played three minutes off the bench against the sixth tier side.

Bristric is taking time getting used to the EFL, but if he remains out of Russell Martin's plans, his value will only decrease.

It's very impressive that Tom Bloxham, at only 23 years old, has 200 EFL appearances, most of which have come in League One. He's been, at worst, a useful squad player for around five years now, at Shrewsbury Town, Morecambe or now at Blackpool.

The towering six-foot-five frontman hasn't properly exploded into a 15-to-20-goal striker just yet in his career, but his duarability and potential contribute to Transfermarkt's value.

Perhaps the new Blackpool boss, once they're in the building, can start to get the best out of him.

Age does, unfortunately, have to play a factor in these values, as if Kyle Wootton was six years younger, he'd easily be worth double. He'd also probably be in the Championship, too.

Instead, the 30-year-old has to settle for being one of the best goalscoring big men in the third tier at Stockport County. He finished second in the Golden Boot ranks last season, but it's arguable that he'd have overtaken Dom Ballard if not for an injury crisis which meant he had to play centre-back for the final month of the campaign.

He's already in double digits this season, and is one of the key reasons why Stockport are so good under Jimmy McNulty, as his aerial threat means that they can go long to him if their patient build-up isn't working. Very valuable to the Hatters, but underrepresented on this list.

A position purely based on potential, Leeds United must be really disappointed that their 18-year-old starlet Harry Gray isn't currently excelling on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, and hasn't yet started a game under new boss Dave Challinor, as of writing.

The England Under-19 international is highly-rated both at Leeds and amongst general footballing circles, with him the latest line of Gray's, who are legendary at Elland Road.

The fact he was loaned out aged just 17 to Rotherham in January, instead of playing more youth football, just shows how developed he already is, and once Gray can finally get clicking at the top end of the pitch, his value will only climb higher.

Welsh international Mark Harris couldn't properly get going at Championship level with Oxford United following his 19-goal campaign in all competitions in 2023/24 to help the Yellows get promoted.

Now he's back in League One, though, his golscoring knack has returned. He's already netted more times than he has in each of his two seasons in the second-tier in the first few months of this term.

Transfermarkt's list shows a green arrow next to his £628k value, too, so it's increased since the start of the season.

Bojan Radulovic's value has definitely increased over the past 12 months or so. His Huddersfield Town career seemed to be over back in January 2025, when he was loaned out to Eredivisie side Fortuna Sittard after playing just 855 minutes of League One action.

He found form back at the Accu Stadium under Lee Grant, though, and netted seven in 15 appearances in the first half of last season. Unfortunately, in 2026, he's had an injury-ravaged year.

Radulovic missed lengthy periods towards the back end of last season, and this year has been in and out of the side under Martin Drury. Nevertheless, he still has a handful of league goals in limited minutes, and a full return would make an already threatening Terriers attack even better.

Someone else whose value has skyrocketed in recent times is Aaron Collins. Plainly put, not many were expecting him to have the year he's currently having based on last season's performances in League Two.

FLW has debated which 15 fanbases generate the best atmospheres and more inside their home stadiums

The 29-year-old was one of the big-money MK Dons captures while they were in League Two, having netted at least 10 in three consecutive third tier seasons, but he only scored six league goals last year.

This season, though, he's scoring a goal a game in all competitions, leading the scoring charts in league action, and was awarded his Wales debut against Portugal in the latest round of Nations League games. Arguably, he could, and should, be even higher.

Jacob Brown was signed by Luton Town back in the summer of 2023 in their first campaign as a Premier League club. He'd netted Championship goals for Stoke City across the previous two seasons.

He's kind of lost his way since, like the Hatters have as a football club, in fairness, and after spending last season on loan up a level in the Championship with Portsmouth, he joined Reading on a free transfer at the end of his contract.

It's been a smart bit of business so far for Reading, with Brown one of, if not the best backup strikers in the division. Almost all of his appearances have been off the bench with Jack Marriott ahead of him, and he's still scored four times in league action as of writing.

#2048. Rangers vs Falkirk - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 14:21

The Scottish Premiership's second and third-placed sides will meet on Saturday, when Rangers welcome Falkirk to Ibrox Stadium.

The hosts are second in the Scottish Premiership standings with 33 points, one point behind leaders Celtic, while the visitors are third with 24 points from 14 matches.

Rangers head into Saturday's match with their sights set on moving to the top of the Scottish Premiership standings for the first time this season.

The Gers trail leaders Celtic by just one point, meaning a victory would lift them above their Old Firm rivals, at least until the Bhoys take on Hearts on Sunday afternoon.

Derek McInnes' men will be full of confidence of claiming all three points, with Rangers heading into the matchday 15 fixture enjoying a sensational 14-game unbeaten run across all competitions.

In the league, Rangers have won 10 and drawn two matches during that run, including winning each of their last three Scottish Premiership fixtures, beating St Mirren 2-0, Motherwell 2-1 and Aberdeen 3-2.

The Gers are also looking to extend their superb record at Ibrox, having won all of their last nine home games, scoring 22 and conceding just four goals in that time.

Despite their fantastic form coming into this match, Rangers will expect a tough test against visitors Falkirk, who travel to Ibrox off the back of six consecutive league triumphs.

That run includes particularly notable wins against Celtic (2-0) and Hearts (5-2), and the Bairns will now be looking to add Rangers' scalp to their collection.

Thanks to those six victories, Falkirk have rapidly ascended to third in the Scottish Premiership standings with 24 points from 14 matches, although they only lead Hearts - who have played one game fewer - by one point.

Alongside their impressive recent run, Falkirk will draw further self belief from their formidable record on the road this season, recording three wins, three draws and suffering just one loss away from home in the league.

John McGlynn's side have, however, failed to defeat Rangers in any of their last seven encounters, including a 2-1 defeat earlier this season.

Rangers are set to be without Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Jose Cifuentes, Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti due to ongoing injuries, while Ross McCrorie is also a doubt with a hamstring injury.

Ryan Don Naderi is Rangers' top scorer in the league with seven goals, and the forward should continue just behind Kevin Kelsy in the forward line.

Falkirk are also contending with several injury absences, including Aidan Nesbitt, Aodhan Doherty, Brad Spencer, Leon McCann and Ryan Strain, while Ethan Laidlaw is a doubt to feature.

Jacob Murrell is Falkirk's top scorer with eight league goals, including seven in his last seven appearances, and the forward will start just ahead of Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames in attack.

Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Bouanani, Naderi, Gassama; Kelsy

Both teams head into this match in fantastic form, leading us to expect a hard-fought encounter. However, given Rangers' formidable Ibrox form and their recent upperhand in this fixture, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

#2047. Chris Wilder urged to make 'controversial' Tom Cannon exit decision at Sheffield United

It has been an excellent start to the season for Sheffield United in the Championship.

After a summer of off-field uncertainty that saw the departures of key players such as Andre Brooks, Callum O'Hare and Gus Hamer, it is fair to say Sheffield United supporters went into the season with low expectations, but Chris Wilder's men have certainly surprised many with their strong start.

After scoring a 90th-minute equaliser to salvage a point in a 1-1 draw with Southampton at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night, Sheffield United are ninth in the Championship table, just one point from the play-off places.

As the Blades continue their impressive form, hopes of a potential promotion push will be increasing in S2, but one man who may not be enjoying his current situation is striker Tom Cannon.

Cannon joined United from Leicester City in January 2025 for a reported fee of around £10 million, but he has scored just 11 goals in 73 appearances during what has been a frustrating near two-year spell at the club.

The 23-year-old has netted three times in 16 games this season, but just nine of those appearances have come from the start, and on what was just his second start in the past month against the Saints in midweek, he was replaced by Patrick Bamford at half time.

Cannon was linked with a return to two of his former loan clubs in the summer, Preston North End and Stoke City, but, speaking in September, the striker denied that he was keen to make a move elsewhere.

When asked which player the club should loan out in January, FLW's Sheffield United fan pundit Jimmy, from the YouTube channel Blades Ramble, claimed that Cannon could benefit from a temporary move, either to boost his confidence ahead of a return to Bramall Lane or increase his value before a potential sale.

"It's slightly controversial this one because I'm not sure how many would agree, but I think that Tom Cannon needs a loan away," Jimmy told FLW.

"Some Blades may have given up on him already and would like to get a fee for him because strikers obviously go for a premium, but I don't think his value would be that high at the moment.

"I think there's potential that he goes elsewhere and does well.

"He could be offered out on loan to the Championship, and then, if he does well, it certainly raises his price, but we would also have the option of bringing him back into the fold at United, where he's still got years to run on his contract.

"He could play a part for us or we could sell him on for a higher price than we'd get now.

"I would be looking at potentially getting Tom Cannon some confidence under his belt by sending him out on loan."

Football League World takes a closer look at the best value-for-money signings in the Championship this season

Despite his underwhelming form throughout his time at the club, Wilder has always been publicly supportive of Cannon, and the Sheffield United boss may be reluctant to give up on a player he has devoted plenty of time to developing.

However, almost two years into his spell at Bramall Lane, Cannon is showing no sign of delivering the prolific form the Blades would have been expecting when they paid an eight-figure fee for his services, so Wilder may soon have a big decision to make.

Does Tom Cannon deserve more time at Sheffield United or should the Blades cut their losses? Tell us in the comments below!

Cannon performed better during his loan stints at Preston and Stoke than he has after his permanent moves to Leicester and Sheffield United, so if the South Yorkshire outfit are keen to recoup some of their money, sending him out on loan could be the perfect way to put him in the shop window.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2046. Real Madrid vs Alaves - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:20

Real Madrid will be aiming to make it 11 straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last nine games against Alaves, including a 2-1 victory in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign.

Real Madrid will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League, with that success making it 10 victories in a row in all competitions.

Jose Mourinho's side are flying, with their winning run including six in Spain's top flight, and they are currently second in the La Liga table, only three points off the leaders Barcelona.

Los Blancos now have three straight league matches against Alaves, Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao before resuming their Champions League campaign away to Arsenal on December 9.

Real Madrid would go level on points with Barcelona should they manage to win this match, and they have been victorious in 38 of their previous 46 games against Alaves in all competitions, suffering only five defeats in the process.

Vinicius Junior is still finding it difficult to show his best form for Real Madrid, but Kylian Mbappe is having another incredible campaign, netting 19 times in 18 appearances in all competitions.

Alaves will be the huge underdogs this weekend, but two of their last three wins over Real Madrid have come away from home, including a 2-1 success at Bernabeu in November 2020.

The Blue and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Deportivo La Coruna, with the result leaving them in ninth spot in the La Liga table on 16 points, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and five defeats from their 13 matches.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have been excellent at home this season, picking up 13 points from seven matches, but they are still waiting for their first away success of the campaign.

Alaves finished 14th in Spain's top flight last season, only one point above the relegation zone, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27.

The Basque outfit will be the fresher of the two teams following Real Madrid's Champions League involvement, but they will be up against a side that have the second-best defensive record (11 conceded) and second-best attacking record (33 scored) during the current season.

Real Madrid will be missing Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg), Ferland Mendy (hip) and Endrick (groin) through injury on Saturday, but no fresh issues have been reported.

There will be changes to the side that took to the field for the first whistle against PSV, with Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen potentially all being introduced into the defence.

Jude Bellingham should also return to the starting side, with Yan Diomande potentially being rested from the first whistle to allow Arda Guler and Vinicius Junior to feature in the wide areas.

As for Alaves, Facundo Garces (knee), Mikel Rodriguez (knee) and Hugo Noava (muscle) are unavailable.

Given the nature of the result and indeed the performance against Deportivo last time out, it is possible that it could be same again in terms of the starting team for the visitors.

Lucas Boye has scored six times in 12 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set to feature in the final third, while Denis Suarez and Antonio Blanco are also set to be in the XI.

Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Tchouameni; Guler, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe

Sivera; Tenaglia, Koski, Otto; Perez, Ibanez, Blanco, Suarez, Rebbach; Martinez, Boye

Alaves deserve credit for what has been a solid season to date, but Real Madrid are in a good place at the moment, and we are fully expecting Mourinho's side to claim another three points.
