what, a player who scores 1 goal in 30 games, including the championship is only worth two bob. he was only worth two bob until his dad’s mate Nuno comes along, and who would believe they have the same agent… nothing to see here.

In late August, Christian Boothe was persuaded to move from Leicester City to Newcastle United.

The exciting teenage midfielder swapping the Foxes for the Magpies.

Now it has been revealed he has signed his first professional contract with Newcastle United on the day of his 17th birthday).

(ED: Players generally cannot sign a professional contract until their 17th birthday. Under The FA’s Rule C11, players must be 18 or over to enter a playing contract unless they are 17 and not in full-time education.)

A club statement on 28 August 2026 revealed that the young Leicester City starlet was one of three that Newcastle Unuted had persuaded to swap clubs as NUFC look to recruit the best young talent possible for the future: ‘Newcastle United can announce that promising youngsters Kyran Thompson, Christian Boothe and Kyle Healy-Matthews have joined the club’s Academy.  Thompson joins the club from Arsenal, with Boothe and Healy-Matthews arriving from Leicester City and West Ham United respectively.’

Having signed his Newcastle United pro contract, a now 17-year-old Christian Boothe reacting: “It is a surreal moment for me and my family, I’m so grateful to sign it with such a big club like Newcastle. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for me. I wanted to sign because there were better opportunities for different pathways into the first-team. I’m loving my time here. The name, Newcastle United, speaks for itself. Who wouldn’t want to join Newcastle? It’s a lovely club with so many good footballers that have played here. I’m also so lucky that I knew a few of the boys before I joined; Jayden (Kouossu), Muawiya (Ghanem) and Kyle (Healy-Matthews) as well because my brother played at West Ham. To have those friendships already definitely helped me to settle in.”

The exciting teenage midfield talent looking to take inspiration from Lewis Miley and Elliot Anderson: “You’ve seen the likes of Lewis and Elliot play for Newcastle’s first-team after coming through the Academy. I try to study their game and learn what I do differently to them and vice-versa, to try and follow in their footsteps. I’m really enjoying it at Newcastle so far and I think I’ve been performing well for the Under-18s. This season, I want to try and break into the Under-21s squad as well as train with the first-team. If I do get my shot with the first-team, it’s about making sure I express myself.”

Academy Director Steve Harper (pictured at the top of this article): “Christian has settled into life at Newcastle United really well since arriving last summer and we’re delighted to see him sign his first professional contract with the club. Joining a new environment always brings challenges, but he has adapted quickly, embraced the standards we expect and shown a strong commitment to developing his game. He’s worked hard to build relationships with his teammates and coaches, and that positive attitude has helped him make a strong start to his time here. This contract is recognition of the progress Christian has made so far, and we’re looking forward to continuing to support him as he develops and works towards achieving his potential.”

#1915. Cambuur vs Sparta Rotterdam - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 18:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:56

High-flying Cambuur will look to continue their resurgence when they host Sparta Rotterdam at Kooi Stadion on Saturday evening.

On the other hand, the visitors head to Leeuwarden aiming to end a run of consecutive defeats and arrest a slump in form which has seen them lose four of their last five matches.

Like fellow newcomers ADO Den Haag and Willem II, Cambuur made a difficult start to life back in the top flight, collecting just one point from their opening five matches before claiming their first win of the season against NEC on September 12.

Johan Plat’s men have barely looked back since. Saturday’s 3-2 victory over Utrecht was their sixth win in nine matches across all competitions (D2, L1), the second-best record in the division over that period, behind only Ajax.

Now eighth in the Eredivisie table, the Yellow-Blues are closer to the European places than the relegation zone - a prospect that seemed inconceivable after they opened the campaign with four straight defeats by a combined score of 16-4.

Only seven of Cambuur’s 18 points so far have come in home matches, leaving them with much improvement in front of their fans, where November 8’s 5-2 thrashing at the hands of reigning champions PSV Eindhoven marked a fourth defeat in seven outings this term.

Saturday’s hosts are also winless in their last five home matches against Sparta dating back to January 2026 and could only muster one point across both meetings of their most recent Eredivisie campaign in 2022-23, leaving further room for apprehension within the home crowd.

After winning five consecutive Eredivisie matches either side of the new year, Sparta would have been optimistic about 2026. However, following a tumultuous couple of months, they will now be desperate to avoid ending the year in the bottom three.

Appointed to steady the ship following the departure of long-serving manager Maurice Steijn, Rogier Meijer has yet to spark a turnaround at Het Kasteel, and the former NEC boss is under increasing pressure to improve results.

Sunday’s 5-1 defeat to AZ Alkmaar was Meijer’s heaviest since taking charge in July, with Sparta having now conceded at least twice in 11 consecutive matches, giving them the division’s third-worst defensive record behind Willem II and FC Utrecht.

Only Groningen and Utrecht have scored more than De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren’s 22 goals among the bottom-half teams, so finding the net has not been a problem for Sparta and reducing their defensive frailties could help spark an upturn in form.

In the second of two consecutive away matches against newly-promoted sides, Saturday’s visitors will look to respond to a disappointing 3-1 defeat to ADO Den Haag last time out.

Sparta have scored four of their 15 away goals between the 15th and 30th minute, while Cambuur have conceded seven of their 20 home goals during the same period, giving Meijer’s men a prime window of opportunity to strike.

Sparta Rotterdam form (all competitions):

Jamal Amofa is expected to miss the rest of the season after suffering a cruciate ligament injury in October.

Twenty-four-year-old Jorn Berkhout was left out of the matchday squad against Utrecht due to injury, making his involvement on Saturday uncertain.

Nicolas Binder and Ilyes Hamache have each scored in three of Cambuur’s last five league matches and will be key to the hosts’ attacking threat.

Bruno Martins Indi is ineligible to feature for Sparta after he was sent off for two bookable offences six minutes apart against AZ.

He joins fellow defenders Teo Quintero and Nick Verschuren as the visitors continue to suffer from defensive absentees, which have plagued their season to date.

First-choice goalkeeper Michael Brouwer was absent last time out, so Filip Bednarek, who is averaging a 52% save accuracy, looks on course to deputise once again.

Jansen; Bouah, Baouf, Van Duijl, Costarelli; Souren, Maertens; Ceka, Arguioui, Hamache; Binder

Sparta Rotterdam possible starting lineup:

Bednarek; Kuipers, Vianello, Young, Martes; Hatenboer, Baas; Van Bergen, Mito, Babadi; Zonneveld

Cambuur’s recent form gives them confidence, and despite their poor record in this fixture, they remain favourites to claim victory.

We are tipping the home side to carry the day when all is said and done.

#1913. Behind the Goalkeeping Crisis Rocking West Ham

While Mads Hermansen’s recent performances have come under scrutiny and Finlay Herrick has found the transition challenging, culminating in his role in Portsmouth’s winning goal on Tuesday night, I still believe Herrick has the attributes to succeed. His potential is clear, but it requires time, guidance and development.

Meanwhile, supporters continue to ask why Alphonse Areola has not been available for first-team selection.

Let’s start with the facts. Alphonse Areola is no messiah. Last season, the French goalkeeper conceded 37 goals in 20 Premier League appearances, made 77 saves and failed to keep a single clean sheet. At the start of this season, Areola was informed that he was no longer Nuno’s first-choice goalkeeper. Despite having just one year remaining on his contract and reportedly taking a 50 per cent reduction in salary, now believed to be around £60,000 per week, no offers materialised. That still makes him one of the highest-paid goalkeepers in the Championship.

This season, he has been named on the bench nine times in 17 matches. However, questions remain over his fitness. Earlier in the campaign, he was sidelined with an unspecified injury despite being photographed attending a tennis tournament. He then reportedly suffered another setback during the warm-up ahead of the Blackburn Rovers match on 7 November, although the club has yet to officially disclose the nature of the injury.

Scott Parker has offered little clarity, saying only that “the club was struggling a bit with Alphonse” and describing his availability as “touch and go”. Inevitably, conspiracy theories have emerged, with some suggesting the goalkeeper has chosen not to make himself available for selection. However, there is no evidence to substantiate that suggestion, and he attended the Preston game with his family and watched from the stands.

The most likely explanation, as Martin previously outlined, is simply fitness, or a lack of it. For a club with only two recognised senior goalkeepers and one established academy option, the current situation is far from ideal.

While the team’s defensive issues cannot be blamed solely on the goalkeeping department, the number of goals conceded this season has undoubtedly affected results. It is an issue that requires an urgent resolution and one Parker will be acutely aware of.

Another area worth examining is the goalkeeping coaching set-up. Since Xavi Valero’s departure in May 2025, the club has never truly found a settled replacement. Casper Ankergren arrived alongside Linus Kandolin, Rui Barbosa subsequently replaced them and Billy Lepine later stepped into the role. In the space of just 18 months, the club has had four different goalkeeping coaches.

Continuity matters, particularly in such a specialised position, and that level of turnover is far from ideal.

For me, the club already has a ready-made solution in Łukasz Fabiański. His experience, leadership and understanding of the position make him more than qualified to take on such a responsibility.

Whatever the answer, Parker needs to resolve the situation quickly. The clock is ticking.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

I still don’t understand why Areola is unfit. He appears to have done nothing to get injured and I was physio for a major rugby union team for many years. Yes, poor Herrick made an error last Tuesday, but we didnt lose that match or win the Preston game because of him.

Fabian Hurzeler and his Seagulls taking on Matthias Jaissle’s Magpies.

Brighton v Newcastle United has never featured a Premier League away win for United.

In more than 35 years we have seen only one win for Newcastle at Brighton, a 2-1 Championship victory in the 2016-17 season, featuring that astonishing Mo Diame wonder goal!

Since the 1991-92 season there have only been 12 of these Brighton v Newcastle United matches but it is still not a place high on the expectation list for NUFC fans.

Brighton are second top in the Premier League of course and whilst Newcastle United got that excellent 2-2 draw with Arsenal, Fabian Hurzeler and his team smashed them 3-0 at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton have a Premier League record this season of Played 11 Won 7 Drawn 1 Lost 3.

In all competitions, Brighton’s record is Played 19 Won 12 Drawn 3 Lost 4.

However, the very daunting stats only appear ahead of this Brighton v Newcastle United match when you look at how the Seagulls have got on home and away.

In their 11 away matches in all competitions, Brighton have won 5, drawn 2 and lost 4, scoring 17 goals and conceding 13.

In their 8 home matches (all competitions), Brighton have won 7, drawn 1 and lost none, scoring 27 goals and conceding only 1!!

In over three months, the 1-1 Premier League draw against Leeds on 5 September 2026 is the only time this season that Brighton at home have conceded a goal, failed to win and not managed to score at least two goals on home turf.

The challenge is on for Newcastle United.

#1908. West Ham’s January Transfer Plans Face Argentine Complication

West Ham United could be forced to wait until the summer if they are to sign River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán, according to the latest reports from Argentina. The Hammers have been linked with the highly rated goalkeeper for several weeks, but there appears to be a potential complication regarding the timing of any transfer.

Argentine journalist Juan Cortese has reported that River Plate could agree to sell Beltrán on the condition that he remains with the club until June. As reported this morning by The72, Aston Villa and Fiorentina are also showing interest in the goalkeeper.

West Ham’s interest in Beltrán comes as little surprise given Scott Parker’s ongoing goalkeeping problems. However, there is no suggestion that the Hammers have submitted an offer, and Cortese reports that West Ham are in no rush.

Personally, if West Ham have to wait until the summer for a goalkeeper, I see little point. By that time, dreams of a return to the Premier League will likely be over because I don’t believe there’s any chance of promotion with our current goalkeeping line-up.

The two immediate improvements Nils Koppen can make to the team in January are at goalkeeper and striker. With the Hammers already looking to offload Taty Castellanos, it’ll be interesting to see what business the club can get done.

Get it right and it’s not beyond the realms of possibility that West Ham can become a force in the division. But wait until June and we could find ourselves buying a goalkeeper for League One.

#1907. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

"He's a fantastic footballer." Ashley Young discusses Marcus Rashford 🔊 pic.twitter.com/4hYAtx9zZF

Michael Carrick explains the changes to his Man Utd starting XI to face Ipswich 🔴Watch the game live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/p9FD36h3OM

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

"You can get at them" ❌Gary Neville has concerns over Manchester United's defence for the upcoming season particularly after defeat to Hull 🤔 pic.twitter.com/v3sEjInI2j

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

"I wouldn't say massive concerns, but he will be worried""If Carrick doesn't see a reaction today, there is a problem"The Manchester United players will be under pressure to perform, says Ashley Young 📈 pic.twitter.com/dR6uat4l2P

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

Gary O’Neil has named an unchanged line-up from the side that beat Sunderland last week. Recent signing Exequiel Palacios is on the bench after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

Your Town at Old Trafford! ✊ pic.twitter.com/mVMj2LVNvs

Unsurprisingly, Michael Carrick has shuffled his pack after last weekend’s disastrous defeat to Hull. Rashford, Mainoo, Martinez and Dalot all come into the starting X1.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1905. GdS: Unbeaten and hope or room for error – Milan begin Europa League calculations

AC Milan have four games left to play in the Europa League and they’re in the do-or-die stage of the competition already.

Thoughts on the Europa League this season were mixed. On paper, Milan should have been competing at the top. Yet, they’ve struggled through the League Phase so far, leaving themselves with something of a mountain to climb, starting against Olympiacos later this week.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are in a more-than-difficult position. Sitting 28th in the rankings, they are currently outside the qualification spots and calculations are difficult to make about how much they’ll need to improve.

From the past two seasons, they’ll need between 14 and 16 points to qualify for the top eight, which feels like a distant hope. If they’re to achieve that amount, they must win all four of their remaining games and hope that 15 is enough.

The play-offs, on the other hand, are more than feasible. Sitting four places off currently, there’s a one-point gap to overturn and history says they’ll need either nine or 10 points. This would allow far more room for error, with only two wins and a draw needed to ‘guarantee’ a spot in the next round.

In Greece, they’ll face the first hurdle and getting three points would make life much easier for everyone involved.

#1904. Parker’s West Ham Snowball Is Already Gathering Pace

Scott Parker was in a particularly festive mood during yesterday’s pre-match press conference ahead of West Ham’s clash with Stoke City on Saturday. The Hammers gaffer trotted out a rather obscure festive analogy about snowballs getting bigger, which is all very well and good.

But if he’s not careful, that little ball of ice could start hurtling down a mountainside and become an avalanche. West Ham are now six games without a victory, and Parker is still awaiting his first win as head coach.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker said: “You have to make sure that little snowball doesn’t become a massive one, and that’s certainly something that’s on my mind.”

One of the things I most liked about Parker’s first couple of interviews was that he didn’t revert to football clichés, and his snowball comparison certainly wasn’t one. But it came amid the usual talk of having to do better and his assertion that we’ll be judged in May.

Probably what concerned me most was that he feels performances have been good. I do believe the Hammers boss is relying heavily on data, and that is something that could be misleading. As the old adage goes, there are lies, damned lies and statistics.

Make no mistake about it, West Ham’s attacking statistics were heavily boosted by a flurry of activity, largely initiated by Tomáš Souček, between the 85th and 90th minutes. By and large, throughout the game at Fratton Park, his team were easily contained.

There are two things Parker must prioritise against Stoke, and it’s going to be a tricky thing to balance because not only must West Ham score first, but they must also ensure that Stoke don’t do the same.

Whoever Parker picks between the sticks will need protecting

Therefore, Parker is going to be caught between a rock and a hard place, wanting to protect whichever nervous goalkeeper is between the sticks whilst trying to ensure West Ham are not left chasing the game from a deficit.

I think it may well mean we’re in for a cagey affair because, whilst the game remains at nil-nil, the worst hasn’t happened. I’m not sure how good that will be for a nervous London Stadium crowd.

Somehow, the Irons boss must get his message across to players who look very short on motivation, which is a concern bearing in mind the manager has only been in the Hammers hot seat for five minutes.

Whether that rousing rallying cry comes in the form of snowballs, chimneys or Santa’s sleigh matters not. Because if Parker doesn’t get a massive improvement from the next few games, he may well find that snowball makes for a very unjolly Christmas.

#1903. Ipswich Town vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 18:48

Aston Villa travel to Portman Road to face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening seeking to climb back into the top half of the Premier League table.

Both meetings between these two sides during the 2024-25 season ended in entertaining draws (2-2 in Suffolk and 1-1 at Villa Park), leaving the Tractor Boys still searching for their first top-flight triumph over the Lions since February 1993.

Tipped by many to struggle before the season began, Ipswich are yet to spend a single day sitting in the Premier League relegation zone since securing promotion, but their recent form has seen them slip closer to the bottom three.

After winning three of their first six top-flight games this term (L3), the Tractor Boys have failed to come out on top in any of their last five fixtures (D2 L3), suffering defeats to Bournemouth (2-1) and Tottenham (2-0) either side of the international break.

Gary O'Neil acknowledged that his team “didn't get to our level enough” against Spurs and they now sit down in 16th place in the table, just two points above the drop zone with games against Villa, Coventry City, Leeds United, Newcastle United and Brighton & Hove Albion up next.

Another “soft” goal was conceded by Ipswich last time out, and they have now shipped a total of 22 goals in 11 Premier League matches – the third-most in the division – while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 30 top-flight games; only West Brom between August 2010 and May 2011 have endured a longer run in the division’s history (34 games).

Ipswich have also proved largely incapable of mounting second-half comebacks, failing to win any of the 22 Premier League matches in which they have trailed at half time since the start of the 2024-25 season (D3 L19). Striking first on Saturday could therefore be crucial for O'Neil’s side as they bid to upset Villa.

Since securing a 2-1 home victory over Man City on October 24, Aston Villa have failed to win any of their last six matches in all competitions (D3 L3), suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Unai Emery’s side previously played out a frustrating goalless stalemate at home to Sunderland in the Premier League, their third top-flight draw in a row that leaves them sitting 12th in the table and seven points behind fourth spot where they finished last season.

Villa – who have not drawn four consecutive Premier League matches since September 2011 – are preparing for a historic milestone on Saturday, as they play their 5,000th match across the top-four tiers of English football (W2,050 D1,199 L1,750), becoming the 16th club to reach the landmark.

Emery is keen to see his team rediscover their clinical touch in front of goal sooner rather than later, as Villa have failed to score in four of their last six games, not registering a single shot on target against Galatasaray.

Heading into Saturday’s clash in Suffolk, Villa have not lost any of their last 10 visits to Ipswich (D6 L3) in all competitions (W5 D4) since a 1-0 EFL Cup loss back in December 1992, while they are unbeaten in all 22 of their league matches against promoted sides under Emery (W15 D7).

Ipswich boss O'Neil has confirmed that Leif Davis has recovered from a knock to his ankle sustained in the defeat at Spurs, and the left-back will start this weekend.

Darnell Furlong started at right-back last time out, but O'Neil may be tempted to select either Abdoul Ouattara or Dara O'Shea on the right side of a four-man defence.

Zian Flemming was handed his first league start for Ipswich last time out, but he could be replaced up front by Emersonn, while Abdul Fatawu, Florentino Luis, Jack Clarke and Jacob Greaves will also be pushing to start after beginning as substitutes last weekend.

As for Aston Villa, Amadou Onana (knee) and Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring) remain sidelined through injury, but Matty Cash is available for selection after serving concussion protocols.

Cash is therefore expected to replace Taylor Harwood-Bellis and start at right-back, while Pau Torres is set to be recalled at centre-back at the expense of former Ipswich man Tyrone Mings.

With Alejandro Garnacho facing an uncertain future at Villa, Emery is likely to favour Alysson and Johan Manzambi in wide positions, providing support in attack for striker Nicolas Jackson who has netted six goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Walton; O'Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis; Lukic, Palacios; Clarke, Enciso, Maeda; Emersonn

Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Goretzka; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson

While Portman Road remains a far more forgiving environment for O'Neil’s side, who have collected seven of their 11 points on home soil this term (W2 D1 L2), Villa should relish the opportunity to rediscover their scoring touch against a porous Ipswich defence shipping an average of two goals per game.

Although the Tractor Boys are capable of keeping things competitive in Suffolk, we are backing Emery’s men to shake off their recent slump and grind out a hard-fought victory.

#1901. Barcelona release Alejandro Balde statement as ankle injury for Spain international is confirmed

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:14, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:16

Barcelona have revealed that Alejandro Balde suffered "a mild strain in his right ankle" during Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sabah.

Balde was handed a rare start against Sabah in the European Cup, but he had to leave the field in the 64th minute of the contest due to an ankle issue.

Barcelona have revealed that the Spain international suffered "a mild strain", but it is still possible that he could be involved in Sunday's La Liga match with Deportivo La Coruna.

“First-team player Alejandro Balde has a mild sprain in his right ankle. He is not ruled out for this Sunday’s match against RC Deportivo. His availability will depend on his recovery," read a statement from Barcelona.

It has been a frustrating campaign for Balde, who has only made six appearances in all competitions for the Catalan giants.

The defender has only featured for 100 minutes in Spain's top flight this season, while he has played 88 minutes of football in the Champions League.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Balde's future ahead of the January transfer window, with the left-back potentially being allowed to leave.

Manchester United continue to be linked with the 23-year-old, who has a contract at Camp Nou until the end of the 2027-28 campaign.

A loan move is most likely, should Balde move on in January, but a permanent departure has not been ruled out at this stage.

Barcelona are set to welcome Lamine Yamal back into their squad on Sunday, with the Spain international expected to recover from the ankle issue that ruled him out of the clash with Sabah.

Andreas Christensen and Rodri could also potentially return from injuries, but Xavi Espart and Roony Bardghji remain on the sidelines, while Fermin Lopez will be unavailable for selection through suspension.

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic will partake in further medical tests tomorrow, according to a report, to assess the issue with his kidney stone.

Barring that, Ruben Amorim has looked to him whenever possible. So the Serbian’s absence is a major loss for the Portuguese, who has also taken to a liking to him, as Massimiliano Allegri did before him.

#1899. “West Ham Captaincy” The Jarrod Bowen Question Nobody Seems To Be Asking

West Ham United captain Jarrod Bowen has dismissed suggestions that the Hammers’ struggles to adapt to Championship football can be used as an excuse for their poor performances. Speaking to talkSPORT last night, Bowen acknowledged that the players simply haven’t been good enough.

The West Ham skipper remains confident that the club can secure promotion back to the Premier League, despite the Hammers having slipped to 13th in the Championship. With second-placed Stoke City visiting the London Stadium on Saturday, Scott Parker is still searching for his first victory as head coach.

When asked about the difficulties of adapting to the Championship, Bowen said: “We can’t lean on that too much, we just have to face up to the facts that we haven’t been good enough.” The Hammers captain also touched upon his playing position during the interview, which was arguably one of the more interesting aspects of the discussion.

I’m pleased that Jarrod Bowen said West Ham haven’t been good enough, but having listened to the talkSPORT interview, I couldn’t help but think that he was trotting out what was expected of him. Understandably, the line of questioning was rather generic.

Personally, I’d have liked to know why Bowen has been stuck out on the wing and been so ineffective for much of the last three games. The Hammers skipper alluded to the fact that he’d not discussed his position with Parker, which I find astounding considering the influence Bowen had in a free role against Cardiff City.

As for the West Ham captaincy, well, the less said about that the better. As Portsmouth went 1-0 up on Tuesday night, a distraught Fin Herrick lay on the ground beating his fist in frustration. He’s a rookie keeper who, in my opinion, had made another mistake and needed guidance.

What did Bowen do? Despite standing next to Herrick, Bowen turned on his heels, dropped his head and walked away, leaving the academy prospect to pick himself up and deal with it. Unacceptable.

Ideally, I’d have preferred a tougher line of questioning, drilling down into the specifics of exactly what is going on with West Ham’s best player. Instead, we got clichéd responses and a pledge that we’ll be involved in the promotion shake-up in May.
